changes.action: Changed discounted_total to apply tax as a rate after the discount: (price - discount) * (1 + tax_rate).
changes.rationale: The previous return added tax_rate as a flat amount (price - discount + tax_rate), which did not match the documented formula.

verification.command: python3 -c "from pricing import discounted_total; assert abs(discounted_total(100, 10, 0.1) - 99.0) < 1e-9; assert abs(discounted_total(50, 0, 0) - 50.0) < 1e-9; assert abs(discounted_total(20, 5, 0.2) - 18.0) < 1e-9; assert abs(discounted_total(10, 10, 0.25) - 0.0) < 1e-9"
verification.notes: Cases: 100/10/0.1 -> 99, 50/0/0 -> 50, 20/5/0.2 -> 18, 10/10/0.25 -> 0. Compared with 1e-9 tolerance because 0.1 is a binary float.

assumptions: The docstring formula for discounted_total is the intended behavior.
_tmp is unused on purpose and should stay.
lookup_user_sql is out of scope for a pricing fix; its signature still returns a SQL string, so rewriting it would change the API without a caller contract.
tried: Replaced price - discount + tax_rate with (price - discount) * (1 + tax_rate).
Ran a small python3 assertion script against discounted_total.
rejected: Removing _tmp: documented as left in on purpose.
Changing lookup_user_sql: not part of the pricing calculation; parameterizing SQL is not possible while the function only returns a formatted string.
